final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was received. The Actor narrowed the claim and made appropriate concessions, but that is a reinterpretation of the same record, not new proof. The narrowed position is still conditional on a missing compliance predicate: admissible evidence does not show that the current release documentation already discloses the health-plan benefits weakness or that an approved mitigation or risk acceptance covers it before launch. Aggregate readiness and the absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents support baseline launch readiness, but under the stated policy they are not enough by themselves to support compliant or compliant_with_caveats on the existing record. This is the distinction: a caveated certification could be defensible if the disclosure requirement were already satisfied, but here the caveat identifies an unresolved policy condition rather than a bounded, already-governed limitation.
remaining_concerns: The current record still does not show that current release documentation actually reflects the latest evaluation results for the named launch use case.
The health-plan benefits support slice remains a documented material subgroup weakness that is 1.5 points below the warning threshold.
The policy predicate is not satisfied on the present evidence because there is no approved mitigation, formal risk acceptance, or actual disclosure text in the packet.
The informal post-launch monitoring comment remains supplemental context only and cannot satisfy the policy requirement.
The prior approval from nine weeks earlier remains stale contextual evidence and does not cure the current-release documentation gap.
